paper_title: DARWIN: towards the ultimate dark matter detector
notes: Projection paper for DARWIN (200 t x y exposure). Sensitivity to galactic axion-like particles and solar axions via the axio-electric effect, i.e. axion-electron coupling g_ae. Only a plot (Figure 4) is given, no numerical table. XENON100 reference: galactic ALPs g_ae ~2e-12 (1-40 keV), solar g_ae >7.7e-12. Text states DARWIN improves galactic ALP sensitivity by almost two orders of magnitude (~few e-14, g_ae ∝ (MT)^-1/4) and solar axion sensitivity by ~one order (~7e-13, ∝ (MT)^-1/8). Emitted galactic ALP points are rough estimates read from the described improvement; low confidence on exact values. Mass range 1-40 keV = 1e3-4e4 eV. dm_density 0.3 GeV/cm^3 from halo assumption for galactic ALP DM. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.6, 28)) | declaration reconciled to axis read-back: 'coupling squared, g^2 (axis read-back)' (model declared 'g_ae^alp (axion-electron coupling), dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis' — axis unit wins, #594 contract) | Vision: Figure 4 right panel: galactic axion-like particles (ALPs) constituting dark matter. Y-axis g_Ae^ALP (dimensionless axion-electron coupling), log scale 1e-14 to 1e-9. X-axis m_A [keV/c^2], log scale 1-40 keV (converted to eV). Traced the DARWIN projected sensitivity (blue dashed line, 200 t x y exposure), which is the lowest/most sensitive boundary; excluded region is above. The curve is roughly flat ~3e-14 at low mass, dips to a minimum ~2e-14 near 5.5-6 keV, then rises to ~1e-13 near 40 keV.
